- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply +1.5–2.5% bias to forecast if sentiment < 0.25.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true price drops sharply, model is lagging; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 0.25), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
